reviews.text: 小丑牌将成功rouge like随机元素融进了棋牌和gambling游戏，使得这些老钱的游戏类型焕发第二春 但是它们无一例外的臭又长并且平衡性崩坏，特别是小丑牌，一着不慎，全盘皆输，做大牌的爽感完全被指数级增长的分数全毁了，build还巨难凑，搞得不是在roll就是在roll的路上，以撒尖塔这些经典rouge like游戏再怎么励志也都是能玩的， Clover Pit则相对回避了这个问题，老虎机roll就完事，不需要考虑局外成长，规划全点在经营就行，随机666时不时还能给空虚堆分的你来点心肺骤停的刺激感 相比demo版本贫瘠build，正式版更新不少新道具，道具池新增的大量道具，使得build更丰富的同时，也让前期变得稍微艰难，嘛，能熬过前两个deadline基本就能利滚利了 不过就目前来说build的广度勉强过关，深度还不够，纯运气流靠demo那几个道具撑腰肯定走不远，需要完全靠左脚踩右脚靠大奖吃饭就能上天的build。 商店的roll机稍微有点过分了，指数级的花费从demo版本留到了现在，只能说没有白嫖绿票，商店很难给人花分roll道具的动力 也许其他地区的人对老虎机不怎么感冒，但对国人而言应该还是蛮新鲜的 小体积低配置，保证办公电脑上班摸鱼没问题，加个窗口可调分辨率模式就更完美了 [spoiler] 37r还是小贵，不过roll爽了就不继续挑剔了 [/spoiler]

上头归上头，但不是因为好玩，是为了体验更多build。游戏难度曲线设计的很差，与其说设计差，不如说制作组压根没思考这块，解锁的道具一股脑塞在一个池子，意味着随着游戏进度＆游玩时间的推进，成型难度会越来越大，前期暴毙几率越来越高，挫败感来的越发频繁，但同时游戏也没有给予玩家一点加强作为平衡，解锁匣子也杯水车薪，最后沦为roll种子的路边肉鸽。游戏难度选择应该给到玩家，允许玩家挑战更高难度，但不能把玩家低难度尝试bd这条路封了。正反馈这块和丝之歌坐一桌的，允许多夹几筷子菜而已。

这是一个控制论游戏而不是道德游戏。当然这取决于你怎么看： 1. 如果你把它看做道德小寓言，那么得出的就是一些“赌狗万劫不复”之类的正确的废话。而更可能的是，这些正确的废话往往是享乐一番后的道德补丁，只是为了让自己心安理得。 2. 如果你把它看做一个控制论游戏，那就有意思了。从宏观上看，整个老虎机系统是一个混沌的输入系统，游戏逼着你还债，这实际上就是逼迫你以各种方式从混沌中构造一个能稳定带来正反馈（盈利）的系统。这样看来，游戏中有“利息”之类的稳定构架，其实就是为了达到这个目标。换言之，每次拉杆可以说都是往系统中输入一组混沌。而真正考验玩家的，不是运气，因为运气也是一种混沌；而是设计一个系统来驯服混沌。这个系统需要提高稳定性，有盈利的预期，并且还要从混沌之中自发地构造起来。这无异于边航行边造船，或者边飞边造机翼。 这与第二序控制论（如 Heinz von Foerster 或 Bateson）提出的系统自组织模型极为相似，在其中： a. 外部扰动是混沌的（老虎机） b. 玩家必须在不完全知识和资源不足下调度结构（构筑build） c. 系统逐步形成反馈环，并“自调节”以维持可生存状态 而最终的问题并不在于你赢了一次或两次，而是从这种游戏中获得一种判断力的提升。它令你能在其他的一些类似场合能保有优势。比如理财或者投资，或者说在新领域展开某种自学，等等。 从这个意义上看，它不是一个赌博游戏，更像是一个理财-投资游戏。而逐步增加的负债只是代表某种强度测试——测试你的交易系统如何在不可控的市场中仍然保持盈利。 当然，你也可以把它当做一个背板游戏，或者纯粹的赌博替代品等等。这就应了一句话：“读《金瓶梅》而生怜悯心者，菩萨也；生畏惧心者，君子也；生欢喜心者，小人也；生效法心者，乃禽兽耳。”——一个客体的意义，有时候完全取决于你怎么对待它。

作为一个策略和轻肉鸽游戏，它过于看中运气了，当你在商店刷到comb的饰品老虎机一分钱不给你的时候，你就知道有多红温，我很少评价游戏，但是这是我第一个玩不下的游戏，过于看重概率的游戏反而失去了随机性的乐趣。我唯一能想到的正面意义就是远离赌博（笑），在我有饰品加持的情况下依然能让我输到半夜通关0次，我会远离赌博的。

最多可以玩到大约玩到第8小时的时候，能解锁所有的抽屉，这就算是游戏全部内容一周目结束了。 此时，死线金额就提高到了"2.1234E+0.6"，这是一个绝对不可能达到的金额，你将会间接性完成不了这次的死线而Game Over。 但这个金额什么时候出现，其实也是随着你玩的次数发生变化的，比如，最一开始你就每一轮过的都很紧张，都是勉强冲线，那么这个死线有可能要第13轮。而随着解锁全部奖励（即四个可以临时存放道具的抽屉），同时又连续3次在新的死线开始时手里就已经持有了超过该死线的金额，那么它会嘲讽你一句：“你有点太顺利了....接下来抽到666的时候，你手里的钱也会归零”。 即便是使用Cheat Engine，由于字节限制，修改后发现持有的现金上限只有999,999,999，也就是说，10位数字的持有现金是不被允许的，因此无法存够"2.1234E+0.6"。 而即便你没有开作弊器，即便你倍数和得分都提高到满，也不过是一回合赚几百万、1000多万，想在3轮达到20亿以上是不可能的。 虽然这个游戏真的很好玩，但我很怀疑它未来更新时能否带来更强的可玩性，因为目前看来，除了做一个能越狱走出大门的结局之外，已经没有什么好更新的了。我相信大部分玩家玩的时候会和我一样，即掌握了一套道具策略后就懒得学习别的了，而这个游戏又恰好把任何一套合理的道具组合都调节的很公平，不存在有唯一无敌的组合。 不过，即便没有眼前一亮的更新，仅凭现阶段的有趣程度，我仍然推荐给新玩家。

Many charms are indeed very situational, and to complete memory packs you will be relying on the same few charms + strategies to consistently win. Despite this, I still find myself booting up the game (whether on steam or on mobile) to play "just one more round" - something about the dopamine rush of running up a massive payout by using the right charms is incredibly satisfying. If you are looking to get the rush of gambling without putting another paycheck on red, I would reccomend this game.

As a non gambler in real life, I strive to find games where I can gamble in the virtual world. The good thing with games is that when you lose, you don't lose any real money. Well you lose time, but that's a different topic. CloverPit has kind of a Squid Game/Saw backstory where you wake up in a cell and have to play a game to survive. It's weird but you quickly accept your fate and carry on with the rules. Everything is explained well and you're encourage to learn through playing and observing your surroundings. There is quite a bit of office humor involved where you can answer calls from your boss for help, look up new stuff on the computer, and of course if you finish paying your debt early, you get a bonus. Funny how it relates to real life yeah? The gameplay loop is quite addicting as you'll find yourself spinning, buying relics, and balancing when to pay all your debt or hold off to gain more coins before cashing in. I can see this one being a game I come back to in the future to unlock even more relics. An easy recommend (just don't try to do this in real life)

This game is a joke, frankly. But I don't know what I expected when it was gifted to me. It takes the least fun part of a roguelike - RNG - and makes it the only mechanic. Roguelikes function not because you're going to get different items each time, they function because you can get better at the game. The RNG exists to round you out, to force you to be able to beat anything the game throws at you. That... is not this game. The skill in this game is ONLY about picking the buffs. The rest of your fate is entirely up to RNG. If you like that, if you enjoy grinding out runs to get the right buffs and sitting at a slot machine forever, AND you can get past the insanely complicated way things are labeled ("permanent" things are not, in fact, permanent at all) and the complete lack of guidance and explanation for most things, then THIS GAME IS FOR YOU! But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it is not for me. I'll probably play every once in a while to get achievements though.

当你基本理解了什么是最优的成长模型后，这个游戏就不再有趣了，当然从零开始去找最优解的过程是有一些意思的。如果5分满分，结合各方面的缺点我只能给到2到3分。缺点一：漫长的动画结算时间，本人最高分数E+51，差点就过了死线18（游戏里第18关），整一局算上中途的一点少量休息，打了十多个小时，绝大部分时间都在看老虎机的结算动画，中途好几次差点睡着，大量无意义的垃圾时间。缺点二：糟糕的UI显示，抽屉里的4个道具，从外边看完全看不到里边装了什么道具，每一次为了找到一个道具往往都要把四个抽屉全部打开一遍。已装备的道具摆放位置极其难看，最多可以装备16个道具，但是很难看清楚其中的每一个道具是否装备上，已装备的道具显示在一共三层的架子上，第三层和第二层都只可以看到3个道具，偏偏第一层放了8个道具，8个道具挤在一块，有的道具被挡住完全看不到，使你没办法快速确认自己装备了哪些道具。缺点三：前期运气成分很大，运营玩法和流派单一。前期找不到刷礼卷的道具和扩音器一局就注定走不远，运气差的时候可能不到十分钟就暴毙了。凑齐道具基本成型后，每回合就是刷老虎机，消耗部分道具后再把消耗的道具买回来，成型阵容就基本只有固定的一套，成型后的道具组合直到游戏结束都不会有太多变化，玩法非常单一。缺点四：令人诟病的通关结局，一个数值游戏的通关方式一般都是到达最终关卡的设定分数后通关，结果设计者告诉你通关和分数没有任何关系（后边看攻略才知道结局怎么完成），当然这一点辩证的来看，把这个游戏当作无尽版游戏玩也完全可以，前提是你准备好看老虎机每一次拉动后漫长的结算动画。最让我无法接受的其实就是漫长的动画结算，第一次打到死线18，不知道这一关的通关分数，准备不充分，差的并不多。本来还想完美营运一把过了死线18，看了一下打到死线18这一局的游戏时间一共14个小时（中途有少量休息没操作），再也不想看动画看到吐，最后就这样结束了这一场开始感觉有点有趣，中途认真思考最优解，最后被迫看几十个小时老虎机重复结算画面的历程（之前也有好几局打了七八个小时）。完成隐藏结局还有其他道具可以解锁，但我已经不再关心了。

I was disappointed by this game. Play Luck be a Landlord instead. The vibe is neat and I appreciate the direction they were going. However, the gameplay is dead boring. The "relics" are fairly basic and unoriginal. The slot gameplay is dull and there's a lot of repetition. The 666 mechanic is just annoying. It feels like the game doesn't respect your time when you do 6 spins and the 7th is a 666. Doesn't feel like you had a choice in risk and reward, just lose what you have and start over. Boring. And frustrating. The last straw for me though was the lack of telegraphing your score. I decided to buy a bunch of Lemon themed relics, got a very high score and up to deadline #10, but throughout the entire run, I really had minimal idea why one spin would get me 150, and another would get me 40,000 coins. I know there are charts on the walls, but there's no way to see the math behind your score result, and thus, felt like I had no agency in the game at all. Also when I beat the game once, I was hoping for a bit of story. You get a black screen that says "the mystery deepens" which feels incredibly patronizing and low effort.

common "buy various items in the shop to increase various numbers that all multiply together to give you a bigger and bigger score" game. features a ticket economy, which is usually solved by a single item, a tiny random chance to spike your cortisol with a 666 and meta progression in the form of unlocking new items for the shop. new run modifiers come in the form of cards; these are limited and you have to GRIND for them (though you get a ton a from a single good run). 100% of your skill comes from luck and knowledge, and is expressed outside the slot machine; you might miss some synergies or items if you dont know about them, but you also just might not get them at all. once you have all drawers unlocked (that is run 5 at the earliest) runs are divided into 3 categories: dead at arrival, dead to bad luck and infinite; some people might enjoy just barely hanging on, but this game presents that experience in the form of being constantly disappointed at the items in the shop. whether its an enjoyable experience depends. the visual design is nice and getting your first jackpot feels great. if you are the type of person that likes sightseeing (that is looking for the mega jackpot after the super jackpot, and looking for E+ after an ultimate jackpot) it all depends on how much time you are willing to sacrifice for your next fix. for me, its not worth it.

Solid roguelike. Watching your score snowball can be super satisfying, and once you understand the mechanics of the game, it's not terribly difficult to do well in most runs. Getting all achievements takes skill and learning but it's not super grindy. I will say, I feel like there isn't a whole lot of variety with the strategy and it mostly always boils down to increasing the chances for a specific symbol and going from there. You can't really get anything out of any charms if you aren't getting patterns, and the way to get patterns is to increase the chances of getting the same symbol, so there's no avoiding that really. Even after ~60 hours and getting all achievements, I feel like I was never pushed to explore new strategies, and there are plenty of charms that I never really used, because they never felt strong/necessary. All in all, it's fun and I enjoyed completing it, but it's not the next Balatro.

Honestly, at first the game is super fun (even after it isn't "fun" it still is tbh). Proves that the concept of gambling is fun even when you aren't gaining anything from winning IRL. The problem is that the whole goal is to increase your chances of winning by using lucky charms that you purchase with tickets you earn while you play. You basically combine perks to try to create an ideal slot machine that consistently pays you out. Some charms are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid, some are really helpful and compound the value of symbols and patterns or give you a "luck" bonus every here and there, or lower the chances of seeing symbols you don't want to see. What sucks is that you don't choose what charms will be available for purchase (6 per round), and you have to pay more and more as the game progresses to re-roll the charms that you can buy, which is still basically just another slot machine, but a way more expensive and disappointing one usually. Additionally, as you play, you unlock more lucky charms, which seems cool at first, but then you realize 99% of the ones you're unlocking will make you lose, so every time you unlock a charm it has a chance of appearing in the store, decreasing the chances of getting the good ones and making your chances of winning go down. It's a fun concept but it would be much more fun if you could choose your favorite charms to increase the chances of them appearing in the store. I was consistently making it to deadline 5+ and the longer I play, the more I'm realizing it's getting harder to make it past deadline 2 or 3. I would recommend it but it's like the game is already based on gambling and winning consistently (duh, basically impossible), but the longer you play, the less likely you are to win, so it becomes IRL gambling where you are trying to turn $16 into $2 mil and it's never going to happen. I was kinda hoping the unlocked charms would actually be good and allow you to win and live out the gambling fantasy lol. I realize now I sound like a gambling addict, I promise I gamble maybe once or twice per year! However, if you don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about winning and just wanna click a button and see how your chances work out, which is objectively fun, the game is pretty damn fun. I almost want to recommend it, but I can't say that I do as someone who likes to figure games out and eventually beat them. It's literally only the fact that it becomes increasingly impossible to beat that turns me away, like reverse RPG leveling. Too bad Steam doesn't offer a number rating system so I could give this a 6/10. Give us the option to select ~30-40 charms that *might* appear in the store and ignore the rest, and this would instantly be a 10/10.
